verdicts.strongest_argument: Every single input to this finding is a number the company itself printed in a shareholder letter, and the second of the two letters is the one that produced a -9.03% reaction. I verified both documents verbatim: the Q4 FY26 letter (2026-03-09) says 'Customers with $50,000 or more of ARR represented $403.6 million or 91% of total ARR' and 'NRR for customers with $50,000 or more of ARR was 99%' / 'NRR was 97% for total customers'; the Q1 FY27 letter (2026-06-02) says 'ARR from customers with annual contract value of $50K or greater was $403.1 million, up 1% year over year', '$50K cohort net retention rate was 97%', 'NRR was 95% for total customers', and 'Total ARR ended the quarter at $440.8 million'. The company does publish the YoY frame rather than the sequential one, so the $403.6m -> $403.1m turn is a derivation -- but it is a one-subtraction derivation between two consecutive letters in the investor-relations tab of a name followed by three analysts, and the broader and more damaging version of the same story (total ARR falling $446.5m -> $444.3m -> $440.8m, sub-$50K ARR -19% YoY, total NRR 95%) was in the wire summary of the June print. The genuinely unpriced part is only the straight-line extrapolation to zero-or-negative YoY in the quarter being reported, and that is a forecast, not a disclosure. It is also the part most likely to be wrong: $403.1m against a $395.3m year-ago base means the cohort can shed $8m sequentially before YoY turns negative, which is a larger step-down than either of the last two quarters produced.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The $111.30m consensus is published -- MarketBeat's own YEXT Q2 FY2027 earnings page carries it alongside $0.17 EPS, and the dailypolitical piece the hunter cites is MarketBeat-syndicated content. But the load-bearing part of the claim is arithmetic, and I think the arithmetic is wrong. The hunter says the only thing bridging $107.92m actual to $111.30m consensus is three extra calendar days. It is not: Q2 FY26 revenue (quarter ended 2025-07-31) was $113.1 million, and Q1 FY26 was $109.5 million, so this company printed a +3.3% Q1-to-Q2 sequential step last year. $107.92m to $111.30m is +3.1% -- the identical seasonal step. Put differently, $111.30m is -1.6% YoY against $113.1m, and Q1 FY27 revenue was -1.4% YoY. The consensus is sitting precisely on the observed YoY decline rate. That is a calibrated estimate, not an uncut one. The claim that estimates 'have not been cut at all' is also contradicted at the analyst-action level: B. Riley Securities downgraded YEXT to Hold and cut its target from $8.00 to $5.00 on 2026-06-03, the day after the miss, and Roth MKM had already cut $9.50 to $6.00 on 2026-03-11. What is left is that a three-analyst blended revenue line has not visibly moved, which on a name with 307 total option contracts of open interest is thin coverage rather than a mispriced bar.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The letter language is exactly as claimed -- I fetched the Q4 FY26 letter and it says verbatim 'We will no longer provide forward-looking financial guidance' and 'We are suspending quarterly earnings conference calls' -- and I also confirmed the 2026-08-18 release mentions no call or webcast. So the finding is factually clean. It is also in the wire copy from the day it happened: TheFly/TipRanks ran 'Yext suspending quarterly guidance' off the 2026-03-09 letter, and it was picked up again in late-March coverage alongside a downgrade. More decisively, the market has now lived through two prints under the new regime -- 2026-03-09 (-2.84%) and 2026-06-02 (-9.03%) -- so no holder is discovering on 1 September that there will be no call and no raise. The analytical overlay ('this removes the mechanism behind the only two up-prints') is a novel framing of known facts, and I do not think it survives its own evidence: the baseline shows 2025-08-18 was a BMO print that went +8.8%, so BMO-plus-no-call is not structurally fatal, and a company that in Q1 FY27 volunteered a GAAP margin range and an EBITDA trajectory has not actually stopped giving forward-looking numbers, whatever the letter says.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The quotes are real -- the Q1 FY27 letter says 'we expect...GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range in Q2, Q3 and Q4' and 'quarterly Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%' -- but 'buried' is not defensible. Both sentences appear in the outlook section of the letter and both were lifted into third-party wire summaries of the 2026-06-02 8-K on the day (StockTitan's write-up carries 'GAAP Net Income margins in the 10-15% range' and 'quarterly Adjusted EBITDA margin expansion towards 30%' as quoted management outlook). It has been public and quotable for 91 days. The arithmetic gap is the part with residual value, and I think the hunter overstates it. Q1 FY27 had Adjusted EBITDA of $26.9m at a 25% margin against GAAP net income of $2.6m -- a $24.3m gap that is mostly SBC, amortisation and interest. Push EBITDA to ~30% of ~$111m, i.e. ~$33m, hold the gap constant, and GAAP net income lands near $9m, or ~8% -- a modest shortfall against a 10% low end, not a company that needs a miracle. And the headline the tape will trade is non-GAAP EPS against $0.17 (MarketBeat) or $0.10 (Zacks) versus $0.15 basic / $0.14 diluted last quarter; a GAAP-margin shortfall against a self-set 'expectation' is a second-order line item on a name with no call, no Q&A and three analysts.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The authorisation arithmetic verifies against the 10-Q -- $14.9m remaining at 2026-04-30, an additional $100.0m authorised by the board in May 2026 as a subsequent event, and 'During the quarter ended April 30, 2026, no repurchases were made under the share repurchase program' -- and the $100m expansion was itself the wire headline on 2026-06-02 (StockTitan: 'Yext posts Q1 FY27 profit and expands $100M share buyback'). The Form 4s are public on filing: EDGAR shows insider filings on 2026-06-12 and 2026-07-13 matching the Waugh and Englander purchases, and the CEO's $9.00 bid was widely reported in 2025. So the entire ex-ante fact set is published. The one genuinely new datum is whether they bought in Q2, and that is a known-unknown of ambiguous sign rather than information. I also think the sign reasoning here is backwards. The reason there were no open-market repurchases in the April quarter is that the company was busy repurchasing 24.3 million shares for $140 million at $5.75 in a modified Dutch auction that closed 2026-03-18, funded by drawing $150m of a $200m BlackRock facility. Management did not decline to buy its own stock; it just spent $140m and most of its debt capacity doing it. That makes an aggressive Q2 open-market program less likely, not more, and it means the $114.9m headroom is closer to a paper authorisation than a coiled bid -- especially with the stock trading well above the $5.75 the company was willing to pay.

adversary_notes: This is a domestic filer whose entire disclosure surface is two documents I fetched and read verbatim, and five of the six findings resolve to language inside them. Both letters check out word for word; I found no fabricated quote anywhere in this brief, which is worth saying. What the brief systematically under-weights is that the 2026-06-02 letter -- the source of h1#0's second data point, h1#4's whole claim and h1#5's authorisation figures -- is the document that already produced a -9.03% reaction. Three findings are re-readings of the same already-traded 8-K. Three factual problems I would flag. (1) h1#1's bridge is wrong: Q2 FY26 revenue was $113.1m, not $107.9m, so the $111.30m consensus is -1.6% YoY against a Q1 FY27 that ran -1.4% YoY, and it replicates last year's +3.3% Q1-to-Q2 sequential step almost exactly. It is a trend-line estimate, not an uncut one. 'Not cut at all' is separately false: B. Riley went Hold with $8 -> $5 on 2026-06-03 and Roth MKM went $9.50 -> $6.00 on 2026-03-11. (2) h1#2 inverts the short-interest story. MarketBeat shows 5.59m shares short at the 2026-08-14 settlement against a 16.85m / 14.4%-of-float peak on 2026-03-13, so shorts covered massively across the rally window; the cited '+7.64% rise' is one fortnight inside that collapse, and days-to-cover is 8.0 on MarketBeat, not 4.63. The finding also omits Needham's still-live Buy and $10.00 target, so 'passed both published price targets' is two of three analysts. (3) h1#5's sign is arguable in the wrong direction. Zero open-market buying in the April quarter is not management refusing to buy; the company repurchased 24.3m shares for $140m at $5.75 via a Dutch auction that closed 2026-03-18, funded by drawing $150m of a $200m facility. With the stock now 19% above the price management was willing to pay and most of the debt capacity spent, $114.9m of headroom is closer to a paper number than a bid. Two structural points cut across everything. First, h1#3 and h1#4 are in direct tension: the brief argues the company has permanently stopped giving forward-looking numbers and, one finding later, that it gave a hard forward numerical bar in the very next letter. Both cannot be the operative frame, and the second is the true one -- Yext dropped the format of guidance, not the substance. Second, the option chain is genuinely dead (307 contracts, 93% ATM spread), so there is no skew or implied move to check any of this against; the only market evidence available is the +20% twenty-day run-up and the -9% June reaction, and every finding here has to be judged against reaction history alone. That argues for compressing the whole set toward the middle rather than trusting any confident reading of what is priced. My aggregate read is that the brief's most valuable residual is not any single claim but the h1#0/h1#4 pair: a cohort ARR line one small step from turning negative, against a self-set GAAP margin range the company will probably undershoot by a couple of points, into a stock up 20% in twenty days with no call in which management can reframe either. That combination is worth something. It is not worth what six separately-sized findings imply, because four of them are the same June 8-K read four ways.
